core_fields.name: deaths

core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Salmonellosis (non-typhoidal Salmonella).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

count_semantics_notes: 'Confirmed cases' in CDC outbreak pages = laboratory-confirmed by culture or WGS

FoodNet counts are laboratory-confirmed isolates reported to surveillance — not outbreak-specific
NORS counts are outbreak-associated cases only — not total disease burden
Hospitalization rates in CDC outbreak summaries are often expressed as percentages of reported cases — compute absolute counts where possible
Death counts in outbreak summaries may be listed as 'deaths reported' without confirmation of Salmonella as direct cause
Probable and suspected case categories are rarely used in US Salmonella reporting — most counts are confirmed or unspecified
State-level case counts may include cases linked to multistate outbreaks already counted in federal totals — flag for deduplication
disambiguation_risks: Salmonella Typhi (typhoid fever) must be excluded — distinct disease, distinct reporting streams
Salmonella in animals or food products without human cases must be excluded
Salmonella serotype names may be confused with geographic place names (e.g., Salmonella Newport, Salmonella Dublin)
Recall announcements may not include confirmed human case counts — distinguish product contamination from human illness reports
FoodNet incidence data is population-based and may not align with outbreak-specific case counts
NORS data may lag real-time outbreak reports by weeks to months
Case counts in news reports may be preliminary and superseded by official final counts
Multi-jurisdiction outbreaks may be reported at both state and federal level — avoid double-counting
Hospitalization and death figures are frequently underreported or reported as ranges

count_semantics_notes: 'Confirmed cases' in CDC outbreak pages = laboratory-confirmed by culture or WGS
'Ill persons' in CDC outbreak pages may include both confirmed and epidemiologically linked cases — clarify before mapping to cases_confirmed vs. cases_unspecified
FoodNet counts are laboratory-confirmed isolates reported to surveillance — not outbreak-specific
NORS counts are outbreak-associated cases only — not total disease burden
Hospitalization rates in CDC outbreak summaries are often expressed as percentages of reported cases — compute absolute counts where possible
Death counts in outbreak summaries may be listed as 'deaths reported' without confirmation of Salmonella as direct cause
Probable and suspected case categories are rarely used in US Salmonella reporting — most counts are confirmed or unspecified
State-level case counts may include cases linked to multistate outbreaks already counted in federal totals — flag for deduplication
disambiguation_risks: Salmonella Typhi (typhoid fever) must be excluded — distinct disease, distinct reporting streams
Salmonella in animals or food products without human cases must be excluded
Salmonella serotype names may be confused with geographic place names (e.g., Salmonella Newport, Salmonella Dublin)
Recall announcements may not include confirmed human case counts — distinguish product contamination from human illness reports
FoodNet incidence data is population-based and may not align with outbreak-specific case counts
NORS data may lag real-time outbreak reports by weeks to months
Case counts in news reports may be preliminary and superseded by official final counts
Multi-jurisdiction outbreaks may be reported at both state and federal level — avoid double-counting
Hospitalization and death figures are frequently underreported or reported as ranges

collection_schema.description: Disease-aware generic public-health collection schema generated for Salmonellosis (non-typhoidal Salmonella) from structured task input and disease intelligence.

core_fields.name: disease
core_fields.description: Standard disease name for the requested task.

core_fields.name: virus_or_syndrome
core_fields.description: Specific pathogen, syndrome, or disease subtype if stated by the source.

core_fields.name: country
core_fields.description: Country where the human cases, deaths, outbreak, or surveillance data occurred.

core_fields.name: subnational_location
core_fields.description: State, province, city, county, district, hospital, or other subnational location as stated.

core_fields.name: date_reported
core_fields.description: Date when the data were reported or published; preserve partial dates when needed.

core_fields.name: event_start_date
core_fields.description: Start date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: event_end_date
core_fields.description: End date of the case event, outbreak, or reporting period if explicitly stated.

core_fields.name: cases_confirmed
core_fields.description: Laboratory-confirmed or source-defined confirmed human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_probable
core_fields.description: Source-defined probable human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths
core_fields.description: Deaths attributed to the reported disease event or surveillance period.

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_id
core_fields.description: Workflow source identifier when available.

core_fields.name: source_url
core_fields.description: URL of the source from which the record was extracted.

core_fields.name: source_type
core_fields.description: Source category used by the data collection workflow.

core_fields.name: evidence_quote
core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id
core_fields.description: Evidence chunk identifier supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Salmonellosis (non-typhoidal Salmonella).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

count_semantics_notes: 'Confirmed cases' in CDC outbreak pages = laboratory-confirmed by culture or WGS
'Ill persons' in CDC outbreak pages may include both confirmed and epidemiologically linked cases — clarify before mapping to cases_confirmed vs. cases_unspecified
FoodNet counts are laboratory-confirmed isolates reported to surveillance — not outbreak-specific
NORS counts are outbreak-associated cases only — not total disease burden
Hospitalization rates in CDC outbreak summaries are often expressed as percentages of reported cases — compute absolute counts where possible
Death counts in outbreak summaries may be listed as 'deaths reported' without confirmation of Salmonella as direct cause
Probable and suspected case categories are rarely used in US Salmonella reporting — most counts are confirmed or unspecified
State-level case counts may include cases linked to multistate outbreaks already counted in federal totals — flag for deduplication
disambiguation_risks: Salmonella Typhi (typhoid fever) must be excluded — distinct disease, distinct reporting streams
Salmonella in animals or food products without human cases must be excluded
Salmonella serotype names may be confused with geographic place names (e.g., Salmonella Newport, Salmonella Dublin)
Recall announcements may not include confirmed human case counts — distinguish product contamination from human illness reports
FoodNet incidence data is population-based and may not align with outbreak-specific case counts
NORS data may lag real-time outbreak reports by weeks to months
Case counts in news reports may be preliminary and superseded by official final counts
Multi-jurisdiction outbreaks may be reported at both state and federal level — avoid double-counting
Hospitalization and death figures are frequently underreported or reported as ranges

collection_schema.description: Disease-aware generic public-health collection schema generated for Salmonellosis (non-typhoidal Salmonella) from structured task input and disease intelligence.

core_fields.name: disease
core_fields.description: Standard disease name for the requested task.

core_fields.description: Specific pathogen, syndrome, or disease subtype if stated by the source.

core_fields.name: country
core_fields.description: Country where the human cases, deaths, outbreak, or surveillance data occurred.

core_fields.name: subnational_location
core_fields.description: State, province, city, county, district, hospital, or other subnational location as stated.

core_fields.name: date_reported

core_fields.name: event_start_date

core_fields.name: cases_suspected
core_fields.description: Source-defined suspected human cases.

core_fields.name: cases_unspecified
core_fields.description: Human cases where confirmation status is not clearly stated.

core_fields.name: deaths

core_fields.name: case_definition
core_fields.description: Case definition or count label used by the source.

core_fields.name: source_type

core_fields.description: Verbatim source text supporting the extracted record.

core_fields.name: supporting_chunk_id

core_fields.name: statistical_count_type
core_fields.description: Count semantics such as cumulative, annual, newly_reported, or point-in-time.

core_fields.name: reporting_period
core_fields.description: Reporting period or temporal aggregation window stated by the source.

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Salmonellosis (non-typhoidal Salmonella).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC DFWED and CDC FoodNet are the primary authoritative sources for confirmed Salmonella case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths in the US. Outbreak investigation pages contain extractable case, death, and hospitalization counts with dates and locations.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify FDA and USDA-FSIS outbreak and recall investigation pages linked to Salmonella cases in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FDA CFSAN and USDA-FSIS publish outbreak and recall investigations that include case counts, implicated food vehicles, and subnational location data relevant to the task window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state health department outbreak reports and press releases for Salmonella in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (all 50 states + DC) publish subnational Salmonella outbreak data, case counts, and epidemiological summaries that may not appear in federal sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MMWR (Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report) articles reporting Salmonella outbreaks or surveillance data for the United States in 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MMWR is a primary CDC publication that contains detailed outbreak reports with confirmed case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and subnational breakdowns for Salmonella events.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent summary or structured sources (e.g., WHO PAHO, ProMED, HealthMap) to compare against collected Salmonella records for the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: International and independent surveillance aggregators provide cross-check data for validation of case counts and outbreak events without being used as primary collection sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FoodNet surveillance data or NNDSS (National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System) structured datasets covering Salmonella in the United States for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FoodNet and NNDSS provide structured, aggregated surveillance data that can serve as independent validation benchmarks for case counts collected from outbreak-specific sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions, FoodNet methodology pages, and PulseNet cluster documentation for Salmonella to support count semantics interpretation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Context sources clarify whether counts are confirmed, probable, suspected, or unspecified; whether they are cumulative or newly reported; and how hospitalizations and deaths are defined.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature (PubMed, MMWR) reporting Salmonella epidemiology, outbreak investigations, or serotype-specific surveillance for the United States in 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Peer-reviewed studies provide case definitions, serotype breakdowns, and epidemiological context that support normalization and interpretation of extracted records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports (e.g., Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today, Reuters) covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may surface early outbreak signals, subnational location details, and implicated food vehicles not yet captured in official reports, supporting collection completeness.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics, mixed cumulative/incident counts, or unclear geographic scope for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources that aggregate multiple outbreaks, span broader time windows, or mix confirmed/suspected counts require human judgment to avoid miscounting or double-counting.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC DFWED, CDC FoodNet, and CDC outbreak investigation pages are the primary authoritative sources for confirmed Salmonella case counts, hospitalizations, deaths, and multistate outbreak investigations in the United States. These pages contain extractable numeric records with dates and subnational locations.

FDA CFSAN outbreak and recall investigation pages and USDA-FSIS outbreak reports contain Salmonella case counts, implicated food vehicles, and subnational location data linked to specific outbreak events in the US.
State health departments publish subnational Salmonella outbreak data, press releases, and epidemiological summaries that provide locality-level case counts not always captured in federal sources.
WHO, PAHO, and ProMED/IMED reports on Salmonella outbreaks in the United States provide independent cross-check data for validation of case counts and outbreak events.
CDC FoodNet surveillance data and NNDSS structured datasets provide aggregated Salmonella case counts by state and time period, serving as independent validation benchmarks.

Peer-reviewed studies and MMWR articles provide case definitions, serotype breakdowns, and epidemiological context for Salmonella outbreaks in the US, supporting normalization and interpretation of extracted records.

Reputable news outlets (Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today, Reuters, AP) and situation reports may surface early outbreak signals, subnational location details, and implicated food vehicles not yet in official reports.

FoodNet incidence data is population-based and may not align with outbreak-specific case counts
NORS data may lag real-time outbreak reports by weeks to months
Case counts in news reports may be preliminary and superseded by official final counts
Multi-jurisdiction outbreaks may be reported at both state and federal level — avoid double-counting
Hospitalization and death figures are frequently underreported or reported as ranges

FoodNet incidence data is population-based and may not align with outbreak-specific case counts
NORS data may lag real-time outbreak reports by weeks to months
Case counts in news reports may be preliminary and superseded by official final counts
Multi-jurisdiction outbreaks may be reported at both state and federal level — avoid double-counting
Hospitalization and death figures are frequently underreported or reported as ranges

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC DFWED, CDC FoodNet, and CDC outbreak investigation pages are the primary authoritative sources for confirmed Salmonella case counts, hospitalizations, deaths, and multistate outbreak investigations in the United States. WHO, PAHO, and ProMED/IMED reports on Salmonella outbreaks in the United States provide independent cross-check data for validation of case counts and outbreak events.
CDC FoodNet surveillance data and NNDSS structured datasets provide aggregated Salmonella case counts by state and time period, serving as independent validation benchmarks.

Peer-reviewed studies and MMWR articles provide case definitions, serotype breakdowns, and epidemiological context for Salmonella outbreaks in the US, supporting normalization and interpretation of extracted records.

Reputable news outlets (Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today, Reuters, AP) and situation reports may surface early outbreak signals, subnational location details, and implicated food vehicles not yet in official reports.

count_semantics_notes: 'Confirmed cases' in CDC outbreak pages = laboratory-confirmed by culture or WGS
'Ill persons' in CDC outbreak pages may include both confirmed and epidemiologically linked cases — clarify before mapping to cases_confirmed vs. cases_unspecified
FoodNet counts are laboratory-confirmed isolates reported to surveillance — not outbreak-specific
NORS counts are outbreak-associated cases only — not total disease burden
Hospitalization rates in CDC outbreak summaries are often expressed as percentages of reported cases — compute absolute counts where possible
Death counts in outbreak summaries may be listed as 'deaths reported' without confirmation of Salmonella as direct cause
Probable and suspected case categories are rarely used in US Salmonella reporting — most counts are confirmed or unspecified
State-level case counts may include cases linked to multistate outbreaks already counted in federal totals — flag for deduplication
disambiguation_risks: Salmonella Typhi (typhoid fever) must be excluded — distinct disease, distinct reporting streams
Salmonella in animals or food products without human cases must be excluded
Salmonella serotype names may be confused with geographic place names (e.g., Salmonella Newport, Salmonella Dublin)
Recall announcements may not include confirmed human case counts — distinguish product contamination from human illness reports
FoodNet incidence data is population-based and may not align with outbreak-specific case counts
NORS data may lag real-time outbreak reports by weeks to months
Case counts in news reports may be preliminary and superseded by official final counts
Multi-jurisdiction outbreaks may be reported at both state and federal level — avoid double-counting
Hospitalization and death figures are frequently underreported or reported as ranges

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Salmonellosis (non-typhoidal Salmonella).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC outbreak investigation pages and active multistate Salmonella outbreak reports for the United States covering May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC DFWED and CDC FoodNet are the primary authoritative sources for confirmed Salmonella case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths in the US. Outbreak investigation pages contain extractable case, death, and hospitalization counts with dates and locations.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify FDA and USDA-FSIS outbreak and recall investigation pages linked to Salmonella cases in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FDA CFSAN and USDA-FSIS publish outbreak and recall investigations that include case counts, implicated food vehicles, and subnational location data relevant to the task window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state health department outbreak reports and press releases for Salmonella in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (all 50 states + DC) publish subnational Salmonella outbreak data, case counts, and epidemiological summaries that may not appear in federal sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MMWR (Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report) articles reporting Salmonella outbreaks or surveillance data for the United States in 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MMWR is a primary CDC publication that contains detailed outbreak reports with confirmed case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and subnational breakdowns for Salmonella events.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent summary or structured sources (e.g., WHO PAHO, ProMED, HealthMap) to compare against collected Salmonella records for the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: International and independent surveillance aggregators provide cross-check data for validation of case counts and outbreak events without being used as primary collection sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FoodNet surveillance data or NNDSS (National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System) structured datasets covering Salmonella in the United States for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FoodNet and NNDSS provide structured, aggregated surveillance data that can serve as independent validation benchmarks for case counts collected from outbreak-specific sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions, FoodNet methodology pages, and PulseNet cluster documentation for Salmonella to support count semantics interpretation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Context sources clarify whether counts are confirmed, probable, suspected, or unspecified; whether they are cumulative or newly reported; and how hospitalizations and deaths are defined.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature (PubMed, MMWR) reporting Salmonella epidemiology, outbreak investigations, or serotype-specific surveillance for the United States in 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Peer-reviewed studies provide case definitions, serotype breakdowns, and epidemiological context that support normalization and interpretation of extracted records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports (e.g., Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today, Reuters) covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may surface early outbreak signals, subnational location details, and implicated food vehicles not yet captured in official reports, supporting collection completeness.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics, mixed cumulative/incident counts, or unclear geographic scope for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources that aggregate multiple outbreaks, span broader time windows, or mix confirmed/suspected counts require human judgment to avoid miscounting or double-counting.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC DFWED, CDC FoodNet, and CDC outbreak investigation pages are the primary authoritative sources for confirmed Salmonella case counts, hospitalizations, deaths, and multistate outbreak investigations in the United States. These pages contain extractable numeric records with dates and subnational locations.

FDA CFSAN outbreak and recall investigation pages and USDA-FSIS outbreak reports contain Salmonella case counts, implicated food vehicles, and subnational location data linked to specific outbreak events in the US.
State health departments publish subnational Salmonella outbreak data, press releases, and epidemiological summaries that provide locality-level case counts not always captured in federal sources.
WHO, PAHO, and ProMED/IMED reports on Salmonella outbreaks in the United States provide independent cross-check data for validation of case counts and outbreak events.
CDC FoodNet surveillance data and NNDSS structured datasets provide aggregated Salmonella case counts by state and time period, serving as independent validation benchmarks.

Peer-reviewed studies and MMWR articles provide case definitions, serotype breakdowns, and epidemiological context for Salmonella outbreaks in the US, supporting normalization and interpretation of extracted records.

Reputable news outlets (Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today, Reuters, AP) and situation reports may surface early outbreak signals, subnational location details, and implicated food vehicles not yet in official reports.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC DFWED, CDC FoodNet, and CDC outbreak investigation pages are the primary authoritative sources for confirmed Salmonella case counts, hospitalizations, deaths, and multistate outbreak investigations in the United States. These pages contain extractable numeric records with dates and subnational locations.

FDA CFSAN outbreak and recall investigation pages and USDA-FSIS outbreak reports contain Salmonella case counts, implicated food vehicles, and subnational location data linked to specific outbreak events in the US.
State health departments publish subnational Salmonella outbreak data, press releases, and epidemiological summaries that provide locality-level case counts not always captured in federal sources.
WHO, PAHO, and ProMED/IMED reports on Salmonella outbreaks in the United States provide independent cross-check data for validation of case counts and outbreak events.
CDC FoodNet surveillance data and NNDSS structured datasets provide aggregated Salmonella case counts by state and time period, serving as independent validation benchmarks.

Peer-reviewed studies and MMWR articles provide case definitions, serotype breakdowns, and epidemiological context for Salmonella outbreaks in the US, supporting normalization and interpretation of extracted records.

Reputable news outlets (Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today, Reuters, AP) and situation reports may surface early outbreak signals, subnational location details, and implicated food vehicles not yet in official reports.

count_semantics_notes: 'Confirmed cases' in CDC outbreak pages = laboratory-confirmed by culture or WGS
'Ill persons' in CDC outbreak pages may include both confirmed and epidemiologically linked cases — clarify before mapping to cases_confirmed vs. cases_unspecified
FoodNet counts are laboratory-confirmed isolates reported to surveillance — not outbreak-specific
NORS counts are outbreak-associated cases only — not total disease burden
Hospitalization rates in CDC outbreak summaries are often expressed as percentages of reported cases — compute absolute counts where possible
Death counts in outbreak summaries may be listed as 'deaths reported' without confirmation of Salmonella as direct cause
Probable and suspected case categories are rarely used in US Salmonella reporting — most counts are confirmed or unspecified
State-level case counts may include cases linked to multistate outbreaks already counted in federal totals — flag for deduplication
disambiguation_risks: Salmonella Typhi (typhoid fever) must be excluded — distinct disease, distinct reporting streams
Salmonella in animals or food products without human cases must be excluded
Salmonella serotype names may be confused with geographic place names (e.g., Salmonella Newport, Salmonella Dublin)
Recall announcements may not include confirmed human case counts — distinguish product contamination from human illness reports
FoodNet incidence data is population-based and may not align with outbreak-specific case counts
NORS data may lag real-time outbreak reports by weeks to months
Case counts in news reports may be preliminary and superseded by official final counts
Multi-jurisdiction outbreaks may be reported at both state and federal level — avoid double-counting
Hospitalization and death figures are frequently underreported or reported as ranges

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Salmonellosis (non-typhoidal Salmonella).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports (e.g., Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today, Reuters) covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may surface early outbreak signals, subnational location details, and implicated food vehicles not yet captured in official reports, supporting collection completeness.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics, mixed cumulative/incident counts, or unclear geographic scope for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources that aggregate multiple outbreaks, span broader time windows, or mix confirmed/suspected counts require human judgment to avoid miscounting or double-counting.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC DFWED, CDC FoodNet, and CDC outbreak investigation pages are the primary authoritative sources for confirmed Salmonella case counts, hospitalizations, deaths, and multistate outbreak investigations in the United States. These pages contain extractable numeric records with dates and subnational locations.

FDA CFSAN outbreak and recall investigation pages and USDA-FSIS outbreak reports contain Salmonella case counts, implicated food vehicles, and subnational location data linked to specific outbreak events in the US.
State health departments publish subnational Salmonella outbreak data, press releases, and epidemiological summaries that provide locality-level case counts not always captured in federal sources.
WHO, PAHO, and ProMED/IMED reports on Salmonella outbreaks in the United States provide independent cross-check data for validation of case counts and outbreak events.
CDC FoodNet surveillance data and NNDSS structured datasets provide aggregated Salmonella case counts by state and time period, serving as independent validation benchmarks.

Peer-reviewed studies and MMWR articles provide case definitions, serotype breakdowns, and epidemiological context for Salmonella outbreaks in the US, supporting normalization and interpretation of extracted records.

Reputable news outlets (Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today, Reuters, AP) and situation reports may surface early outbreak signals, subnational location details, and implicated food vehicles not yet in official reports.

NORS data may lag real-time outbreak reports by weeks to months

count_semantics_notes: 'Confirmed cases' in CDC outbreak pages = laboratory-confirmed by culture or WGS
'Ill persons' in CDC outbreak pages may include both confirmed and epidemiologically linked cases — clarify before mapping to cases_confirmed vs. cases_unspecified
FoodNet counts are laboratory-confirmed isolates reported to surveillance — not outbreak-specific
NORS counts are outbreak-associated cases only — not total disease burden
Hospitalization rates in CDC outbreak summaries are often expressed as percentages of reported cases — compute absolute counts where possible
Death counts in outbreak summaries may be listed as 'deaths reported' without confirmation of Salmonella as direct cause
Probable and suspected case categories are rarely used in US Salmonella reporting — most counts are confirmed or unspecified
State-level case counts may include cases linked to multistate outbreaks already counted in federal totals — flag for deduplication
disambiguation_risks: Salmonella Typhi (typhoid fever) must be excluded — distinct disease, distinct reporting streams
Salmonella in animals or food products without human cases must be excluded
Salmonella serotype names may be confused with geographic place names (e.g., Salmonella Newport, Salmonella Dublin)
Recall announcements may not include confirmed human case counts — distinguish product contamination from human illness reports
FoodNet incidence data is population-based and may not align with outbreak-specific case counts
NORS data may lag real-time outbreak reports by weeks to months
Case counts in news reports may be preliminary and superseded by official final counts
Multi-jurisdiction outbreaks may be reported at both state and federal level — avoid double-counting
Hospitalization and death figures are frequently underreported or reported as ranges

extraction_rules: Extract only human public-health records about Salmonellosis (non-typhoidal Salmonella).
Keep confirmed, probable, suspected, unspecified, death, hospitalization, and surveillance metrics separate when the source distinguishes them.
Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC outbreak investigation pages and active multistate Salmonella outbreak reports for the United States covering May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: CDC DFWED and CDC FoodNet are the primary authoritative sources for confirmed Salmonella case counts, hospitalizations, and deaths in the US. Outbreak investigation pages contain extractable case, death, and hospitalization counts with dates and locations.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify FDA and USDA-FSIS outbreak and recall investigation pages linked to Salmonella cases in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FDA CFSAN and USDA-FSIS publish outbreak and recall investigations that include case counts, implicated food vehicles, and subnational location data relevant to the task window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state health department outbreak reports and press releases for Salmonella in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (all 50 states + DC) publish subnational Salmonella outbreak data, case counts, and epidemiological summaries that may not appear in federal sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MMWR (Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report) articles reporting Salmonella outbreaks or surveillance data for the United States in 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MMWR is a primary CDC publication that contains detailed outbreak reports with confirmed case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and subnational breakdowns for Salmonella events.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent summary or structured sources (e.g., WHO PAHO, ProMED, HealthMap) to compare against collected Salmonella records for the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: International and independent surveillance aggregators provide cross-check data for validation of case counts and outbreak events without being used as primary collection sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FoodNet surveillance data or NNDSS (National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System) structured datasets covering Salmonella in the United States for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FoodNet and NNDSS provide structured, aggregated surveillance data that can serve as independent validation benchmarks for case counts collected from outbreak-specific sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions, FoodNet methodology pages, and PulseNet cluster documentation for Salmonella to support count semantics interpretation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Context sources clarify whether counts are confirmed, probable, suspected, or unspecified; whether they are cumulative or newly reported; and how hospitalizations and deaths are defined.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature (PubMed, MMWR) reporting Salmonella epidemiology, outbreak investigations, or serotype-specific surveillance for the United States in 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Peer-reviewed studies provide case definitions, serotype breakdowns, and epidemiological context that support normalization and interpretation of extracted records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports (e.g., Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today, Reuters) covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may surface early outbreak signals, subnational location details, and implicated food vehicles not yet captured in official reports, supporting collection completeness.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics, mixed cumulative/incident counts, or unclear geographic scope for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources that aggregate multiple outbreaks, span broader time windows, or mix confirmed/suspected counts require human judgment to avoid miscounting or double-counting.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC DFWED, CDC FoodNet, and CDC outbreak investigation pages are the primary authoritative sources for confirmed Salmonella case counts, hospitalizations, deaths, and multistate outbreak investigations in the United States. These pages contain extractable numeric records with dates and subnational locations.

FDA CFSAN outbreak and recall investigation pages and USDA-FSIS outbreak reports contain Salmonella case counts, implicated food vehicles, and subnational location data linked to specific outbreak events in the US.
State health departments publish subnational Salmonella outbreak data, press releases, and epidemiological summaries that provide locality-level case counts not always captured in federal sources.
WHO, PAHO, and ProMED/IMED reports on Salmonella outbreaks in the United States provide independent cross-check data for validation of case counts and outbreak events.
CDC FoodNet surveillance data and NNDSS structured datasets provide aggregated Salmonella case counts by state and time period, serving as independent validation benchmarks.

Peer-reviewed studies and MMWR articles provide case definitions, serotype breakdowns, and epidemiological context for Salmonella outbreaks in the US, supporting normalization and interpretation of extracted records.

Reputable news outlets (Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today, Reuters, AP) and situation reports may surface early outbreak signals, subnational location details, and implicated food vehicles not yet in official reports.

query_batch.query: CDC Salmonella outbreak investigation 2024 cases hospitalizations deaths United States May June July
query_batch.query_rationale: CDC is the primary US federal authority for Salmonella surveillance. Its outbreak investigation pages and MMWR reports are the highest-trust source for confirmed case counts, hospitalization rates, deaths, and subnational location breakdowns. Targeting CDC directly without rigid quoting maximizes recall of relevant pages published in or covering May–July 2024.

query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain, MMWR publication, official outbreak investigation notice

query_batch.query: FDA Salmonella outbreak recall advisory 2024 cases United States May June July food vehicle
query_batch.query_rationale: FDA issues outbreak advisories and recall notices for food-vehicle-linked Salmonella outbreaks, often including case counts, affected states, and hospitalization data. query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: FDA outbreak advisory pages, FDA food safety alerts, FDA recall notices with epidemiological data
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: fda.gov domain, official outbreak advisory or recall notice with case count data

query_batch.query: Salmonella multistate outbreak United States 2024 cases deaths hospitalizations state health department

Avoiding exact-phrase quoting improves recall across varied agency naming conventions.

query_batch.expected_trust_signal: State .gov domains, ProMED archive, PAHO PAHO.int, named public health official quotes with case counts

count_semantics_notes: 'Confirmed cases' in CDC outbreak pages = laboratory-confirmed by culture or WGS
'Ill persons' in CDC outbreak pages may include both confirmed and epidemiologically linked cases — clarify before mapping to cases_confirmed vs. cases_unspecified
FoodNet counts are laboratory-confirmed isolates reported to surveillance — not outbreak-specific
NORS counts are outbreak-associated cases only — not total disease burden
Hospitalization rates in CDC outbreak summaries are often expressed as percentages of reported cases — compute absolute counts where possible
Death counts in outbreak summaries may be listed as 'deaths reported' without confirmation of Salmonella as direct cause
Probable and suspected case categories are rarely used in US Salmonella reporting — most counts are confirmed or unspecified
State-level case counts may include cases linked to multistate outbreaks already counted in federal totals — flag for deduplication
disambiguation_risks: Salmonella Typhi (typhoid fever) must be excluded — distinct disease, distinct reporting streams
Salmonella in animals or food products without human cases must be excluded
Salmonella serotype names may be confused with geographic place names (e.g., Salmonella Newport, Salmonella Dublin)
Recall announcements may not include confirmed human case counts — distinguish product contamination from human illness reports
FoodNet incidence data is population-based and may not align with outbreak-specific case counts
NORS data may lag real-time outbreak reports by weeks to months
Case counts in news reports may be preliminary and superseded by official final counts
Multi-jurisdiction outbreaks may be reported at both state and federal level — avoid double-counting
Hospitalization and death figures are frequently underreported or reported as ranges

Do not infer missing values or calculate derived metrics unless explicitly stated in the source.
Every extracted record must preserve source_url, source_type, evidence_quote, and supporting_chunk_id when available.
Preserve reporting_period, as_of_date, statistical_count_type, geographic_scope, and geographic_scope_type when the source states count semantics or aggregate geography.
Current extraction record model remains HantavirusRecord; unsupported target fields are retained in schema planning with warnings.

count_semantics_notes: 'Confirmed cases' in CDC outbreak pages = laboratory-confirmed by culture or WGS
'Ill persons' in CDC outbreak pages may include both confirmed and epidemiologically linked cases — clarify before mapping to cases_confirmed vs. cases_unspecified
FoodNet counts are laboratory-confirmed isolates reported to surveillance — not outbreak-specific
NORS counts are outbreak-associated cases only — not total disease burden
Hospitalization rates in CDC outbreak summaries are often expressed as percentages of reported cases — compute absolute counts where possible
Death counts in outbreak summaries may be listed as 'deaths reported' without confirmation of Salmonella as direct cause
Probable and suspected case categories are rarely used in US Salmonella reporting — most counts are confirmed or unspecified
State-level case counts may include cases linked to multistate outbreaks already counted in federal totals — flag for deduplication
disambiguation_risks: Salmonella Typhi (typhoid fever) must be excluded — distinct disease, distinct reporting streams
Salmonella in animals or food products without human cases must be excluded
Salmonella serotype names may be confused with geographic place names (e.g., Salmonella Newport, Salmonella Dublin)
Recall announcements may not include confirmed human case counts — distinguish product contamination from human illness reports
FoodNet incidence data is population-based and may not align with outbreak-specific case counts
NORS data may lag real-time outbreak reports by weeks to months
Case counts in news reports may be preliminary and superseded by official final counts
Multi-jurisdiction outbreaks may be reported at both state and federal level — avoid double-counting
Hospitalization and death figures are frequently underreported or reported as ranges

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify FDA and USDA-FSIS outbreak and recall investigation pages linked to Salmonella cases in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FDA CFSAN and USDA-FSIS publish outbreak and recall investigations that include case counts, implicated food vehicles, and subnational location data relevant to the task window.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify state health department outbreak reports and press releases for Salmonella in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: State health departments (all 50 states + DC) publish subnational Salmonella outbreak data, case counts, and epidemiological summaries that may not appear in federal sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify MMWR (Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report) articles reporting Salmonella outbreaks or surveillance data for the United States in 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: MMWR is a primary CDC publication that contains detailed outbreak reports with confirmed case counts, deaths, hospitalizations, and subnational breakdowns for Salmonella events.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify independent summary or structured sources (e.g., WHO PAHO, ProMED, HealthMap) to compare against collected Salmonella records for the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: International and independent surveillance aggregators provide cross-check data for validation of case counts and outbreak events without being used as primary collection sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC FoodNet surveillance data or NNDSS (National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System) structured datasets covering Salmonella in the United States for 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: FoodNet and NNDSS provide structured, aggregated surveillance data that can serve as independent validation benchmarks for case counts collected from outbreak-specific sources.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify CDC case definitions, FoodNet methodology pages, and PulseNet cluster documentation for Salmonella to support count semantics interpretation.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Context sources clarify whether counts are confirmed, probable, suspected, or unspecified; whether they are cumulative or newly reported; and how hospitalizations and deaths are defined.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify peer-reviewed literature (PubMed, MMWR) reporting Salmonella epidemiology, outbreak investigations, or serotype-specific surveillance for the United States in 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Peer-reviewed studies provide case definitions, serotype breakdowns, and epidemiological context that support normalization and interpretation of extracted records.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Identify reputable news and situation reports (e.g., Food Safety News, Outbreak News Today, Reuters) covering Salmonella outbreaks in the United States during May–July 2024.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: News sources may surface early outbreak signals, subnational location details, and implicated food vehicles not yet captured in official reports, supporting collection completeness.

source_discovery_objectives.objective: Flag sources with ambiguous count semantics, mixed cumulative/incident counts, or unclear geographic scope for human review before extraction.
source_discovery_objectives.rationale: Sources that aggregate multiple outbreaks, span broader time windows, or mix confirmed/suspected counts require human judgment to avoid miscounting or double-counting.

planned_source_categories.why_relevant: CDC DFWED, CDC FoodNet, and CDC outbreak investigation pages are the primary authoritative sources for confirmed Salmonella case counts, hospitalizations, deaths, and multistate outbreak investigations in the United States. These pages contain extractable numeric records with dates and subnational locations.

FDA CFSAN outbreak and recall investigation pages and USDA-FSIS outbreak reports contain Salmonella case counts, implicated food vehicles, and subnational location data linked to specific outbreak events in the US.
State health departments publish subnational Salmonella outbreak data, press releases, and epidemiological summaries that provide locality-level case counts not always captured in federal sources.
WHO, PAHO, and ProMED/IMED reports on Salmonella outbreaks in the United States provide independent cross-check data for validation of case counts and outbreak events.
CDC FoodNet surveillance data and NNDSS structured datasets provide aggregated Salmonella case counts by state and time period, serving as independent validation benchmarks.

Peer-reviewed studies and MMWR articles provide case definitions, serotype breakdowns, and epidemiological context for Salmonella outbreaks in the US, supporting normalization and interpretation of extracted records.
